chapters.title: Chapter 146: A Loving Wife Rage | They Shouldn’t Have Dared
paragraphs: Hearing her name, Selene paused before releasing a quiet breath.
A satisfied smile lingered on her lips as she slowly closed the ancient book resting in her hands.
Without turning around, she calmly spoke.
"Come in."
Her enchanting voice drifted toward the door.
Click.
With a soft sound, the exquisitely carved wooden door slowly opened.
Standing at the entrance was a beautiful young woman in her mid-twenties.
Her long black hair flowed gracefully to her waist, while her crimson eyes remained fixed on Selene, carrying a trace of concern.
Rosalyn Bloodbane.
A fallen noble who had been assigned to serve Selene ever since childhood.
Over the years, the bond between the two had become far more than that of mistress and servant.
They were close friends. Trusted companions.
Though within Emperyan Academy, Rosalyn officially served as Selene’s teaching assistant, helping her with lectures and academy affairs.
"My Lady."
Hearing the familiar gentle voice, Selene finally turned around.
The moment she saw Rosalyn standing there, a warm smile naturally bloomed across her face.
It had been an entire month since Rosalyn had left the academy on an assignment.
"Rosalyn." Selene softly called her name.
Rosalyn smiled in return.
However...
Her expression quickly turned serious.
"Miss..."
"I’ve brought news regarding Luke Voidheart."
The warmth on Selene’s face instantly disappeared.
A handsome face unconsciously surfaced within her thoughts.
Deep blue eyes. Messy black hair.
Luke.
Soon afterward...
The memories of the Holy Light Temple replayed one after another.
The awkward conversations.
The quiet moments they had shared.
Their brief time together.
And their loving night.
’How are you...?’
’Have you been eating properly?’
’...Did you miss me?’
One question after another quietly appeared within her heart.
Without realizing it...
She became lost in those memories.
"Ahem."
Rosalyn deliberately coughed.
The sound immediately pulled Selene back to reality.
Blinking once, Selene lightly shook her head before the gentle smile returned to her face.
"What’s the news?"
"Tell me."
Still smiling softly, she gracefully rose from her chair before walking toward the bed.
Curiosity flickered in her crimson eyes.
After sitting down, she gently patted the empty space beside her, inviting Rosalyn to join her.
Rosalyn politely shook her head.
Remaining where she stood, she began recounting the latest news that was currently spreading across the continent like wildfire.
Selene listened quietly.
One hand supported her chin while a faint smile remained on her lips.
Especially when she heard that Luke had already reached the Early Bronze Knight realm.
Although slightly surprised...
She felt genuinely happy for him.
However...
When Rosalyn mentioned that Luke had defeated a Mid-Golden Knight with a single punch...
Even Selene’s expression froze.
"Are you certain?"
A trace of disbelief appeared in her eyes.
"I want to believe it..."
"But rumors can easily be fabricated."
"Many people intentionally spread false information to manipulate public opinion."
She paused briefly.
’Has Luke really reached that level...?’
’It’s only been fourteen days.’
Rosalyn understood her doubts.
She nodded confidently.
"I’ve already verified it through multiple sources."
"It’s one hundred percent true."
Hearing that...
The smile gradually returned to Selene’s face.
’It seems...’
’He really has become much stronger.’
A quiet sense of relief filled her heart.
But...
That peaceful atmosphere lasted only until Rosalyn mentioned one particular name.
The Hidden Hand.
The smile vanished. with that an icy chill spread throughout the room.
"I thought..."
"...that by remaining here..."
"...my family would leave him alone."
Her voice became frighteningly calm.
"But it seems..."
"...others have grown bold enough to target him as well."
Selene slowly raised her head.
Her crimson eyes deepened into a terrifying blood-red.
Sharp vampire fangs gradually emerged.
An overwhelming pressure silently filled the room.
Seeing the sudden change, Rosalyn immediately grew anxious.
"My Lady."
"Please calm yourself."
"Luke Voidheart is unharmed."
"And now that the news has spread..."
"I’m certain they won’t dare attack him again."
Rosalyn tried her best to comfort her.
Unfortunately...
The words achieved the exact opposite effect.
"They won’t dare?"
Selene slowly tilted her head.
Her voice had become colder than winter itself.
"They..."
"...shouldn’t."
Rosalyn instinctively took one step backward.
Only a handful of times in her life had she seen Selene this furious.
And every one of those occasions had ended with rivers of blood.
"How many branches do we currently have on the Human Continent?"
Selene’s cold voice echoed through the room.
She was referring to...
The Crimson Crown.
The assassination organization she had personally founded during the years she endured oppression from her royal family.
Its members consisted entirely of vampires fiercely loyal to her.
Although its headquarters lay hidden within the Vampire Continent...
Its influence extended into nearly every major race’s territory.
Including the Human Continent.
Rosalyn answered honestly.
"We currently maintain one hundred branches there."
"The strongest among them is a High Vampire."
A High Vampire. Equivalent to a Platinum Knight. One full realm above a Golden Knight.
Selene narrowed her eyes.
She quietly fell into thought.
Several moments later...
She finally reached a decision.
"For now... Reject every new assassination request."
"Then issue an new order."
"I want every Crimson Crown branch on the Human Continent..."
"...to hunt down every single member of the Hidden Hand."
Rosalyn’s eyes widened.
"My Lady!" She almost cried out.
"Our influence on the Human Continent is far weaker than theirs."
"If we openly declare war on their home ground..."
"Our branches could suffer catastrophic losses."
"There is even a chance of complete annihilation."
Her voice was filled with genuine concern.
"My Lady..."
"Please reconsider."
"Our forces simply aren’t strong enough."
Selene’s gaze remained ice cold.
"Then..."
"Should I remain silent..."
"...while they attempt to murder my husband?" Her voice suddenly rose.
Rosalyn instinctively flinched upon this.
Something about Selene had changed after returning from the Holy Light Temple.
She could feel it.
The Selene standing before her... Was no longer exactly the same as before.
’What truly happened inside the temple...?’ Before Rosalyn could think further...
Selene spoke again. "Don’t worry."
"I’m not foolish enough to issue such an order without preparation."
Hearing that, Rosalyn finally breathed a small sigh of relief.
Perhaps...
Her Lady had already devised another plan.
Then Selene calmly continued.
"Send reinforcements from our main stronghold to the Human Continent."
"I want only one outcome."
She slowly stood.
Her blood-red eyes glowed with terrifying intent.
"Which..."
"...the annihilation of every lower-ranking member of the Hidden Hand."
Realizing that any further words would be useless, Rosalyn simply nodded with a weary expression.
Without saying anything else, she quietly left the room.
Click.
The door closed softly behind her.
Watching Rosalyn leave, Selene took a slow, deep breath to calm herself.
Gradually, the crimson glow in her eyes faded back to normal, and her sharp fangs slowly retracted.
After regaining her composure, she gathered several notebooks along with her enchanted quill.
Then, without another word, she left the room and headed toward the lecture hall.
And I am very gratefull for that, So please continue supporting this novel, like you are doing now.
Thank you very much.

"Luke Voidheart is unharmed."
"And now that the news has spread..."
"I’m certain they won’t dare attack him again."
Rosalyn tried her best to comfort her.
Unfortunately...
The words achieved the exact opposite effect.
"They won’t dare?"
Selene slowly tilted her head.
Her voice had become colder than winter itself.
"They..."
"...shouldn’t."
Rosalyn instinctively took one step backward.
Only a handful of times in her life had she seen Selene this furious.
And every one of those occasions had ended with rivers of blood.
"How many branches do we currently have on the Human Continent?"
Selene’s cold voice echoed through the room.
She was referring to...
The Crimson Crown.
The assassination organization she had personally founded during the years she endured oppression from her royal family.
Its members consisted entirely of vampires fiercely loyal to her.
Although its headquarters lay hidden within the Vampire Continent...
Its influence extended into nearly every major race’s territory.
Including the Human Continent.
Rosalyn answered honestly.
"We currently maintain one hundred branches there."
"The strongest among them is a High Vampire."
A High Vampire.
Equivalent to a Platinum Knight.
One full realm above a Golden Knight.
Selene narrowed her eyes.
She quietly fell into thought.
Several moments later...
She finally reached a decision.
"For now...
Reject every new assassination request."
"Then issue an new order."
"I want every Crimson Crown branch on the Human Continent..."
"...to hunt down every single member of the Hidden Hand."
Rosalyn’s eyes widened.
"My Lady!" She almost cried out.
"Our influence on the Human Continent is far weaker than theirs."
"If we openly declare war on their home ground..."
"Our branches could suffer catastrophic losses."
"There is even a chance of complete annihilation."
Her voice was filled with genuine concern.
"My Lady..."
"Please reconsider."
"Our forces simply aren’t strong enough."
Selene’s gaze remained ice cold.
"Then..."
"Should I remain silent..."
"...while they attempt to murder my husband?" Her voice suddenly rose.
Rosalyn instinctively flinched upon this.
Something about Selene had changed after returning from the Holy Light Temple.
She could feel it.
The Selene standing before her...
Was no longer exactly the same as before.
’What truly happened inside the temple...?’ Before Rosalyn could think further...
Selene spoke again.
"Don’t worry."
"I’m not foolish enough to issue such an order without preparation."
Hearing that, Rosalyn finally breathed a small sigh of relief.
Perhaps...
Her Lady had already devised another plan.
Then Selene calmly continued.
"Send reinforcements from our main stronghold to the Human Continent."
"I want only one outcome."
She slowly stood.
Her blood-red eyes glowed with terrifying intent.
"Which..."
"...the annihilation of every lower-ranking member of the Hidden Hand."
Realizing that any further words would be useless, Rosalyn simply nodded with a weary expression.
Without saying anything else, she quietly left the room.
Click.
The door closed softly behind her.
Watching Rosalyn leave, Selene took a slow, deep breath to calm herself.
Gradually, the crimson glow in her eyes faded back to normal, and her sharp fangs slowly retracted.
After regaining her composure, she gathered several notebooks along with her enchanted quill.
Then, without another word, she left the room and headed toward the lecture hall.
And I am very gratefull for that, So please continue supporting this novel, like you are doing now.
Thank you very much.

chapters.title: Chapter 147: The Jealous Vampire | Damn You, Luke
paragraphs: While Selene was passing through the corridor, which was enormous and stretched for hundreds of meters, countless students from different races walked back and forth.
Elves, dragons, vampires, humans, mermaids, winged people, giants, beastkin, dwarves, spirits, and many more.
The wide corridor was lined with towering white pillars engraved with ancient runes, while massive crystal chandeliers floated near the ceiling, illuminating the entire area with a soft golden glow.
Large glass windows revealed floating islands outside, where students could be seen flying on, griffins, magical beasts, and even enchanted artifacts.
Everywhere, lively conversations echoed.
Some students laughed together.
Some hurried toward their classes.
Others were engaged in magical discussions, while a few practiced spells by creating tiny flames, water droplets, or floating swords above their palms.
Despite the crowd, the academy maintained remarkable order.
No one dared to cause trouble openly.
Because Emperyan Academy was one of the few places on Valtharion that had survived the Shadow Era—the age when the gods had vanished and chaos consumed the entire world.
Kingdoms had fallen.
Civilizations had disappeared.
Countless races had gone extinct.
Yet this academy had endured through it all.
And now it had become one of the strongest existences in the Dusk Era, which was also known as the Hero Era.
The era in which a Hero was summoned every one thousand years to stand against the Demon race.
Because of Emperyan Academy’s near-invincible strength and its ancient history, almost every race sent their children here.
Among them were not only talented commoners but also countless nobles.
Princes. Princesses. Young masters of ancient clans. Successors of legendary bloodlines. Future kings.
The academy had also produced extraordinary results throughout history.
Many of its graduates had risen to stand at the very peak of the world.
Not one.
But countless.
Some became rulers.
Some became legendary generals.
Some became Hero companions.
While others reached heights that ordinary people could never even imagine.
Because of that, gaining admission into Emperyan Academy had become one of the fiercest competitions in the entire world.
Even a single vacant seat was enough to make countless geniuses fight desperately for it.
And the academy had always maintained absolute neutrality.
It belonged to no kingdom. No empire. No race. No religion.
It sided with no one.
Its laws were equally applied to every student.
Its famous principle was known throughout the world.
"Everyone is equal under the Emperyan roof."
Whether noble or commoner.
Whether human or dragon.
Whether vampire or elf.
Whether male or female.
Inside these walls...
Everyone possessed the same rights.
And everyone received the same punishment.
Unfortunately...
Very few truly accepted that ideal.
Pride built over thousands of years could not disappear overnight.
As a result, numerous factions had formed throughout the academy.
Some gathered according to race.
Others according to noble status.
Ancient clans stayed with their own.
Royal families rarely mingled with commoners.
Even rival races often glared at one another whenever they crossed paths.
It wasn’t uncommon to see dragons looking down on other races.
Or vampires refusing to share a table with werewolves.
Although open discrimination was strictly forbidden, subtle conflicts and silent rivalries had never disappeared.
This was also one of the reasons Selene had chosen this place.
After graduating from the academy, she worked tirelessly and eventually became one of its professors, granting her complete protection from her Vampire royal family.
As Selene walked through the grand hall, countless eyes instinctively turned toward her.
Not only because of her strength.
But also because of her breathtaking beauty.
Her flawless features, graceful bearing, and captivating figure could rival even that of a succubus—the enchanting demon race renowned for seducing hearts with their unmatched charm.
For a brief moment, conversations quieted.
Many male students couldn’t help but steal another glance before quickly looking away.
Some stood frozen in place.
Others whispered among themselves.
"Professor Selene..."
"She’s even more beautiful up close."
"I can’t believe she’s a vampire."
"Don’t keep staring. She’ll notice."
"I heard hundreds confessed to her during her student days."
"And every single one was rejected."
Meanwhile, several female students admired her elegant appearance.
Some viewed her as an idol.
Others envied the effortless grace with which she carried herself.
Even a few professors smiled and greeted her with respectful nods as she passed.
Because of all this, regardless of race, nearly every male student in Emperyan Academy had fantasized about her at least once.
And thanks to her gentle, approachable personality, she had become the most popular professor among the academy’s newer students.
Yet despite the admiration surrounding her, Selene paid no attention to the countless gazes fixed upon her.
With calm, elegant steps, she simply continued toward her destination, her serene expression never changing.
Marius Duskraven, a vampire noble who had been a professor at Emperyan Academy for several years...
Had always harbored feelings for Selene.
When he first heard that she had married the Hero, his heart shattered into countless pieces.
Fortunately...
It recovered the very next day.
Because news quickly spread that the Hero she had married had been declared talentless.
For the first time in days, Marius had smiled.
His rival had become a joke.
But before he could properly celebrate...
His freshly repaired heart shattered once again.
He had heard rumors that Selene and Luke had entered the Holy Light Temple together.
For any married couple, the meaning was obvious.
’I curse you, Hero... May your both balls be annihilated!’
That day, Marius repeated the curse thousands of times.
Ironically...
It happened to be the exact same day Luke’s both balls had nearly been crushed by Aurielle’s hands.
Fortunately for Luke...
Marius never learned about that incident.
Otherwise, he would have doubled the number of curses without hesitation.
Now, standing inside the academy corridor, Marius watched Selene walk past.
His lips parted slightly.
He wanted to greet her.
Yet not a single word came out.
’Damn you, Luke.’
So he silently cursed him again.
Ever since yesterday, his mood had been terrible.
The reason was simple.
News had spread throughout the world that Luke had slain a Mid-Golden Knight.
Not only that...
The so-called talentless Hero had apparently proven everyone wrong.
’Impossible!’
’It’s all lies!’
’You’re definitely talentless!’
’Damn you, Luke!’
So he cursed him once more.
"Huff..."
Taking a deep breath, Marius tried to calm himself.
Only then did he notice several nearby students staring at him strangely.
Apparently...
His face had become bright red while he was silently cursing Luke.
’Ahem...’ Pretending nothing had happened, he adjusted his robe with a dignified expression.
Then, after a brief moment of thought...
’Should I curse him one more time...?’
He seriously considered it.
A few seconds later, he shook his head.
’Forget it.’
’Why should I waste my time thinking about a crippled man?’
Yes.
A crippled man.
Recently, Marius had learned that Selene’s step-brothers and step-sisters had somehow discovered that she creating an hidden organization, which had her strength increased considerably.
Naturally, that made them uneasy.
If Selene became too powerful, controlling her would become impossible.
So they had reportedly decided upon the simplest solution.
Cripple Luke.
As long as the Hero became powerless, Selene would have little choice but to return under the royal family’s influence.
’Damn yo—’
He forcibly stopped himself.
With a smile that looked far more confident than he actually felt, Marius began walking after Selene.
’Today is our joint lecture.’
’This time...’
’I will definitely win her heart with my profound knowledge, refined elegance, and irresistible charm.’
Thinking that, he couldn’t help but feel that the weather was unusually pleasant today.
Unfortunately for him...
He had forgotten one very important detail.
This was not the first time he had reached that exact conclusion.
Nor the second.
Nor even the tenth.
And every previous attempt had ended in complete failure.

chapters.title: Chapter 148: Previously Chosen Dragon Bride For Luke
paragraphs: THUD!
With a deafening impact, the colossal body of a thousand-foot-tall Stone Giant crashed onto the earth.
The ground trembled violently.
Mountains of dust shot into the sky as countless cracks spread across the battlefield.
Floating beside the fallen giant was a woman with brilliant golden draconic eyes.
Her long crimson hair danced in the wind, cascading gracefully to her waist, while a double black dragon horn curved proudly from the both side of her forehead.
An overwhelming draconic aura surrounded her, causing the surrounding space to ripple faintly.
"Tch... Another weakling."
Rhaenyra clicked her tongue in dissatisfaction before sweeping her gaze across the battlefield.
Everywhere she looked.
Corpses.
Thousands upon thousands of Stone Giants lay scattered across the devastated land.
Each one radiated the lingering pressure of a Platinum Knight.
Mixed among them were the charred remains of demons, many of whom had reached the Diamond Knight realm.
The battlefield resembled a graveyard.
"If none of you are strong..."
"...then why the hell does every one of you keep invading my territory?"
Her annoyance grew with every passing second.
The next moment.
WHOOSH!
Scarlet dragon fire erupted from her palm.
The terrifying flames engulfed the battlefield.
The giant stone bodies melted into rivers of molten rock within moments, while the demon corpses were reduced to ashes without leaving behind even a bone.
Only scorched earth remained.
"Rhaenyra."
A calm voice suddenly called from behind.
Hearing it, Rhaenyra turned around, her golden draconic eyes narrowing slightly.
Yes.
She was Luke’s third wife.
Rhaenyra Crimsonscale.
The daughter of the Dragon King.
And the granddaughter of the Dragon Emperor.
"What?" she asked impatiently as she looked toward the newcomer.
Standing behind her was a young woman with long snow-white hair that reached her thighs.
Crystal-like dragon horns extended elegantly from both sides of her head, while her icy blue draconic eyes remained as calm as a frozen lake.
Her younger sister.
Emberlyn Starfall.
According to dragon tradition.
The Hero should have married Emberlyn.
After all, she was the youngest unmarried princess among the Dragon King’s daughters.
Originally, Rhaenyra had also been considered.
Unfortunately.
Emberlyn had become far too powerful.
Rather than sending one of his strongest daughters away, the Dragon King had simply chosen the weakest eligible princess instead.
"When I become even stronger."
"I’ll personally snap both of that old geezer’s horns."
Rhaenyra muttered under her breath.
Unfortunately for her.
Emberlyn heard every single word.
She merely sighed.
This certainly wasn’t the first time her elder sister had threatened to beat their father.
Nor would it be the last.
As for their surnames.
Why was one called Crimsonscale while the other was Starfall?
The reason was simple.
Among dragons—and many noble families possessing ancient bloodlines—their true family names were absurdly long.
Even after shortening them, they remained difficult to pronounce.
Because of that, dragons simply referred to one another by the final part of their lineage title, which usually represented their dragon type.
Otherwise.
Emberlyn’s even small name would be something like.
Emberlyn Xarzith’Drevab Starfall.
Compared to that.
Simply calling her "Starfall" was far easier.
Emberlyn looked directly into Rhaenyra’s eyes before calmly delivering the message she had brought.
"Father has summoned you."
The moment she heard those words.
Rhaenyra’s expression darkened.
Ever since returning from the Holy Light Temple, she had repeatedly asked that old geezer to remove the golden chains restricting her freedom.
She refused to live like a caged beast.
More importantly.
She refused to marry someone weaker than herself.
Yet every single time.
The Dragon King had answered with only one word.
"Later."
And now.
He was calling her back.
"...Fine."
Although clearly dissatisfied, Rhaenyra eventually nodded.
The next instant.
ROOOOAR!!
Brilliant crimson flames and icy-white light erupted simultaneously.
Their human forms disappeared.
In their place appeared two enormous dragons whose wings blotted out the sky.
With a single powerful flap.
BOOM!
The surrounding mountains shook as both dragons shot into the sky, flying toward the distant mountain range whose towering peaks seemed to touch the very edge of Valtharion’s sky.
After traveling for a few hours, they finally landed on the peak and transformed back into humanoid form, which was surprisingly not covered by snow.
Instead, all types of luxurious jewelry, treasure, gold and many rubies were spread around, like dirt.
’That geezer couldn’t even clean his house.’ Rhaenyra’s face turned to disgust.
Even though most dragons like to collect shiny and costly things, she didn’t like it. Only strength mattered to her.
While Emberlyn’s expression didn’t change much, and she remained calm throughout the journey.
Soon they reached the colossal palace, made entirely of gold, and entered through the huge gate.
Far in the distance.
A humanoid figure stood silently atop a huge throne.

Two magnificent crystal horns extended from his head, while his long silver-white hair flowed behind him like a celestial river. Faint purple starlight shimmered throughout his hair, making it appear as though countless stars had been woven into it.
His pair of eyes resembled miniature galaxies.
Endless stars revolved within them.
If Luke had been present, he would have been greatly shocked.
Because the man’s appearance bore an uncanny resemblance to Luke’s Cosmic Heart Titan transformation.
"You took long enough."
His mature voice, carrying the weight of thousands of years, calmly reached both sisters.
"Greetings, Father."
Emberlyn gracefully lifted the edge of her skirt before bowing with flawless etiquette.
Astron smiled faintly at his youngest daughter’s manners before shifting his gaze toward his elder daughter.
"Hmph."
"Why have you summoned me, you old geezer?"
Hearing her greeting.
He simply sighed helplessly.
Most dragons naturally inherited personalities influenced by their elemental affinity.
Astron’s element was Astral.
The power of the cosmic energy itself.
As a result, he possessed a calm, patient, and thoughtful temperament.
Emberlyn, on the other hand, possessed three elemental affinities.
Frost. Crystal. Light.
Fortunately, all three granted her a composed and graceful personality.
She rarely lost her temper, regardless of the situation.
’But.’
Astron glanced toward Rhaenyra.
Her burning golden eyes and flowing crimson hair reflected her draconic lineage perfectly.
She was a Fire Dragon.
Hot-blooded. Proud. Impatient.
And irritated by almost everything.
Because of that very personality.
When his wife had proposed marrying Rhaenyra to the newly summoned Hero, Astron had agreed without much hesitation.
Originally.
The marriage had been intended for Emberlyn.
However, he changed his decision at the last moment.
Perhaps.
Marriage would calm Rhaenyra’s fiery temperament.
Instead.
She had abandoned her husband.
Astron’s expression darkened slightly.
The next moment, it returned to normal.
He couldn’t entirely blame her.
After all.
The Hero had been publicly declared talentless.

While Emberlyn’s expression didn’t change much, and she remained calm throughout the journey.
Soon they reached the colossal palace, made entirely of gold, and entered through the huge gate.
Far in the distance.
A humanoid figure stood silently atop a huge throne.
Two magnificent crystal horns extended from his head, while his long silver-white hair flowed behind him like a celestial river.
Faint purple starlight shimmered throughout his hair, making it appear as though countless stars had been woven into it.
His pair of eyes resembled miniature galaxies.
Endless stars revolved within them.
If Luke had been present, he would have been greatly shocked.
Because the man’s appearance bore an uncanny resemblance to Luke’s Cosmic Heart Titan transformation.
"You took long enough."
His mature voice, carrying the weight of thousands of years, calmly reached both sisters.
"Greetings, Father."
Emberlyn gracefully lifted the edge of her skirt before bowing with flawless etiquette.
Astron smiled faintly at his youngest daughter’s manners before shifting his gaze toward his elder daughter.
"Hmph."
"Why have you summoned me, you old geezer?"
Hearing her greeting.
He simply sighed helplessly.
Most dragons naturally inherited personalities influenced by their elemental affinity.
Astron’s element was Astral.
The power of the cosmic energy itself.
As a result, he possessed a calm, patient, and thoughtful temperament.
Emberlyn, on the other hand, possessed three elemental affinities.
Frost.
Crystal.
Light.
Fortunately, all three granted her a composed and graceful personality.
She rarely lost her temper, regardless of the situation.
’But.’
Astron glanced toward Rhaenyra.
Her burning golden eyes and flowing crimson hair reflected her draconic lineage perfectly.
She was a Fire Dragon.
Hot-blooded.
Proud.
Impatient.
And irritated by almost everything.
Because of that very personality.
When his wife had proposed marrying Rhaenyra to the newly summoned Hero, Astron had agreed without much hesitation.
Originally.
The marriage had been intended for Emberlyn.
However, he changed his decision at the last moment.
Perhaps.
Marriage would calm Rhaenyra’s fiery temperament.
Instead.
She had abandoned her husband.
Astron’s expression darkened slightly.
The next moment, it returned to normal.
He couldn’t entirely blame her.
After all.
The Hero had been publicly declared talentless.

chapters.title: Chapter 149: The Conflicted Heart Of Luke Dragon Wife
paragraphs: ’I still tried.’
That was precisely why, when Rhaenyra had asked him to remove the restraints placed upon her after returning from the Holy Light Temple.
He had simply answered, "Later."
"Huff..." Astron exhaled slowly to steady himself.
Unfortunately. His peace lasted only a single second.
"Why are you sighing so much today, you old geezer?"
"I think it’s about time you handed your throne over to me."
Astron’s eyelids twitched.
Meanwhile.
Rhaenyra looked completely serious.
She showed no intention of stopping now that she had begun.
Still. Astron understood the reason behind her unusual behavior.
For several days after returning from the Holy Light Temple, she had behaved normally.
Then. Without warning.
Her emotions had begun fluctuating wildly.
She became irritated far more easily than before.
Thinking of those memories, Astron looked at Rhaenyra with his glowing, galaxy-like eyes.
The next moment. Invisible chains wrapped tightly around Rhaenyra’s heart became visible before his gaze.
Countless divine runes glowed faintly across every link.
’The chains forged by the Goddess of Light.’ Astron’s brows furrowed.
’But... why?’
’What reason would a goddess have for doing this?’
’Could some greater scheme be unfolding?’
One possibility after another surfaced in his mind.
Yet after a brief moment... He dismissed every one of them.
’The scheme of gods are beyond the understanding of mortals.’
Whether they acted for salvation. Or destruction.
Only they knew the truth.
Astron withdrew his gaze before calmly looking back at Rhaenyra.
"Regarding your previous request."
"I have agreed."
"Really?" Rhaenyra’s eyes immediately lit up.
For the first time in a long while, genuine happiness appeared on her face.
If the chains were broken.
She would finally regain her freedom.
No longer would she have to live like a caged beast.
However. The next sentence from Astron instantly shattered her excitement.
"Unfortunately, I cannot break those chains myself."
"As they contain Divinity."
His voice remained calm, almost indifferent, confusing Rhaenyra.
’You just said you accepted my request.’ But next moment her thoughts abruptly stopped.
’Divinity?’
Her eyes widened slightly before she looked toward her father.
He was smiling.
’Old geezer.’ She silently cursed him once again.
"As you already know, Divinity is a power that only gods..."
"...and demigods can wield."
"So, I will ask your grandfather to remove those chains instead."
"And you don’t need to worry about any backlash."
"However." The moment Astron mentioned her grandfather, Rhaenyra’s smile returned.
The Dragon Emperor personally taking action.
There was nothing to worry about.
But the instant Astron paused.
Her eyes narrowed. ’This old geezer definitely has an ulterior motive.’
Astron naturally noticed the suspicious look she was giving him.
It was almost as if she were staring at a swindler trying to lure an innocent child with candy.
’This little rascal.’ He inwardly sighed.
In the past, he could easily tolerate her antics.
But ever since those divine chains had begun affecting her emotions.
Every conversation with her became twice as exhausting.
Suppressing the twitch on his face, he calmly continued.
"In exchange."
"You must protect one territory for an entire year."
"And before that year ends."
"You will eliminate every monster nest within its borders."
On this Rhaenyra merely smiled. Because she never once considered the possibility that her father would assign her an impossible task.
As far as she was concerned. It was nothing more than another routine mission.
Standing quietly nearby, Emberlyn listened to everything with her usual calm expression.
However. When the conversation shifted toward the Hero.
A trace of curiosity finally appeared in her eyes.
Originally. She had been the one chosen to marry him.
Although she had never cared whether the Hero was talented or not.
After all. She was already stronger than nearly everyone of her generation.
Even many older dragons couldn’t compare to her.
"Rhaenyra." Astron suddenly smiled. "Have you heard the recent news about your husband?"
At those words. Rhaenyra’s smile gradually faded.
An image unconsciously surfaced in her mind.
A cute young man. Black hair. Deep blue eyes.
If Luke ever discovered that Rhaenyra considered his Manly appearance...
Cute.
He would probably suffer more emotional damage than from any battlefield.
Thump.
Her heartbeat skipped. At the same time.
The invisible chains wrapped around her heart tightened once again.
She frowned.
She hated that sensation. She hated feeling forced. And more than anything.
She hated becoming attached to someone weaker than herself.
Yet strangely. Her father’s words had sparked a small trace of curiosity.
Even she didn’t understand why.
"What news?" Her voice remained as indifferent as ever.
Astron smiled before calmly revealing everything.
"Luke had never been talentless.
"He had already reached the Early Bronze Knight realm without receiving support from any empire."
"Not only that."
"He had even slain a Mid-Golden Knight despite the enormous difference in strength."
"Huh?" For the first time, a genuine surprise appeared on Rhaenyra’s face.
’Then...’
’Why did the Saintess lie?’
And this question confused her mind.
Before she could think further.
Astron’s voice interrupted her thoughts.
"So do you still wish to have those chains removed?"
He paused briefly before adding,
"Because Luke is no longer talentless."
"If those chains are broken now."
"He will lose nearly twenty percent of his talent."
"His cultivation will decline."
"And even his foundation will suffer irreversible damage."
Silence.
Rhaenyra froze. Her expression gradually became conflicted.
She looked at her father. Then lowered her gaze.
After several long moments. Without answering a single question.
She silently turned around and walked away. She never looked back.
Emberlyn watched everything quietly.
Even her usually calm face revealed a hint of surprise.
A moment later. Her expression returned to normal.
She respectfully bowed toward Astron before following after her elder sister.
The enormous palace doors slowly closed behind them.
"Sigh..."
Another weary sigh escaped Astron’s lips.
He had genuinely believed that after hearing of Luke’s achievements...
Rhaenyra would immediately decide to remove the chains.
Yet. She had left without giving him an answer.
He didn’t know whether that silence should be considered good news...
Or bad.
Perhaps.
It meant she had begun developing feelings for her husband.
Or perhaps.
Her silence itself was already the answer.
Only she knew.
"I can only hope." Astron murmured quietly while gazing toward the endless stars beyond the palace.
"that the Hero..."
"...can tame the flames burning within my daughter’s heart during these one year."
With those final words. The palace fell silent once more.
Astron slowly closed his galaxy-like eyes and returned to his slumber.
A slumber spent searching the boundless cosmos.
For the ancient truths of an forgotten era long erased from history.

chapters.title: Chapter 150: Naivara Tidewhisper Feels Everything Beautiful
paragraphs: Naira (Naivara Tidewhisper) was traveling aboard a magic train.
It was the fastest way to reach the nearest coastal island.
From there... They could finally return home.
The Ocean.
Outside the train, majestic mountain ranges stretched endlessly beneath the clear sky, while rivers shimmered like silver ribbons between the valleys.
The train itself carried passengers from many races.
Humans. Elves. Dwarves. and Beastkin.
Merchants loudly discussed business deals.
While children ran through the aisles before being pulled back by their parents.
Occasionally, the distant laughter of adventurers drifted through the corridors.
Although the they had reserved an entire private coach...
The muffled chatter outside still reached the cabin.
Yet.
Naira heard none of it.
She was completely absorbed in the newspaper resting in her hands.
More precisely.
The article about Luke. News of his accomplishments had spread across the world like wildfire.
’You’ve become strong.’ A gentle smile unknowingly appeared on her lips.
And the more she read. The brighter that smile became.
Before long, memories of the time they had spent together quietly surfaced within her heart.
Without realizing it.
She lowered her gaze toward the ring on the ring finger of her left hand.
The silver band reflected the warm sunlight entering through the window.
’You are my wife.’
’And this is proof.’
Luke’s smiling face vividly appeared in her mind as he had spoken those words.
"Idiot." A soft giggle escaped her lips. Along with a faint blush gradually spread across her cheeks.
’I hope you’ll come soon.’ and this thought quietly echoed through her heart.
"Luke..."
"...My husband."
Whispering those words so softly that only she could hear them, Naira gently rested her forehead against the window.
Her sapphire eyes watched the magnificent mountains rush past.
The endless forests, clear rivers, and the floating clouds.
For some reason.
Everything looked more beautiful than before.
And somehow she felt that everything would eventually be alright.
Across from her.
Oryn silently watched the smile on Naira’s face.
His fists slowly clenched. While the veins on the back of his hands bulged slightly.
’Damn it!’
’She’s definitely thinking about that low-life.’ He silently cursed Luke.
Earlier, his personal guards had also informed him about the Hero’s recent achievements.
Initially he had only been surprised.
But after learning that Luke had supposedly killed a Mid-Golden Knight with a single punch.
Surprise turned into shock. And shock gradually became fear.
Fortunately he had already left the Count’s territory.
Otherwise if Luke somehow discovered that he had been secretly manipulating events alongside Demon Whisper.
Things could become troublesome.
Though what Oryn didn’t know. Was that Luke had already uncovered the truth. Naira knew as well.
The only reason neither of them had acted. Was because of Oryn’s status.
For now they simply waited.
Waiting for the perfect opportunity to settle everything at once.
Meanwhile, Oryn’s guards noticed the ugly expression twisting across their young master’s face.
However not a single one of them dared to comment.
They merely stood quietly beside the cabin entrance.
Beside them stood Naira’s royal guards. Both groups remained completely silent.
Only the rhythmic sound of the magic train echoed through the carriage as it continued its journey toward the endless sea.
Elves Continent...
In the heart of the continent stood a colossal World Tree.
Its massive trunk pierced the heavens, disappearing beyond the clouds, while its countless branches stretched across the entire Elven Continent.
Each leaf was as large as a small island.
Together, they formed an endless emerald canopy that sheltered the entire continent beneath its shade.
Entire cities had been built upon those gigantic leaves.
Elegant bridges of living vines connected one leaf to another, while crystal-clear rivers flowed naturally through the branches, creating a paradise unlike any other.
At the very base of the World Tree rested an enormous royal palace.
It had been woven entirely from the World Tree’s sacred leaves.
Although it appeared delicate. Its defenses were anything but.
Every leaf possessed unimaginable toughness. Only the absolute peak powerhouses of Valtharion could even hope to damage them.
Inside one of the palace’s grand corridors.
Elf maids moved gracefully from room to room.
Royal knights silently patrolled the halls.
Scholars carried ancient scrolls, while attendants busied themselves with their daily duties.
Everything proceeded in perfect order.
Suddenly.
One young elf maid rushed through the corridor.
Her long blonde hair fluttered behind her as she hurried toward the palace’s inner chambers.
The area reserved exclusively for the royal princes and princesses.
Many servants paused briefly.
Several knights raised their brows.
"...Lyra?"
"What’s the hurry?"
"Did something happen?"
A few whispered among themselves.
However the curiosity quickly disappeared. Everyone recognized her.
Lyra.
One of Princess Elaria’s personal maids.
If she was in such a hurry. It was undoubtedly related to the princess.
Lyra noticed the numerous gazes following her. But she didn’t stop.
She continued running as quickly as palace etiquette allowed.
Then her footsteps abruptly halted.
Someone had blocked her path.
Standing before her was a handsome young elf with long golden hair flowing neatly behind his back.
Unlike Lyra’s soft and radiant hair.
His possessed an elegant nobility that naturally accompanied royal blood.
His emerald eyes calmly looked down at her.
Prince Haldir.
"Y-Your Highness..."
"H-Highness Haldir..."
Lyra nervously lowered her head. Her voice trembled slightly.
Although she herself was an elf. She wasn’t born into the Royal Bloodline.
And Prince Haldir had never hidden his disdain toward common-born elves.
Fortunately Haldir paid little attention to her frightened expression.
InsteadhHis gaze settled upon the folded newspaper clutched tightly in her hands.
’A newspaper?’ His eyes narrowed slightly.
Recently even he had heard whispers regarding the Human Continent.
More specifically the sudden rise of Luke Voidheart.
The Hero once ridiculed as talentless.
And the husband of his younger stepsister.
Princess Elaria.
Judging by Lyra’s destination, she was obviously rushing to deliver the news.
"What is written in that paper?" His voice remained calm.
Yet the contempt directed toward Lyra was impossible to miss.
The young maid instinctively flinched.
For several moments, She hesitated.
Her fingers tightened around the newspaper until it nearly crumpled.
Finally gathering her courage, she answered quietly.
